hardware: AMD RYZEN AI MAX+ PRO 395 / Radeon 8060S (laptop form factor: variable power/clocks; gross numbers only, not for single-digit-percent differentiation)
purpose: External kernel survey plus GEMV leaf bandwidth microbench to decide whether an optimization pass is warranted.

pwilkin/strix-halo.finding: Website/installer project (index.html, install.sh); contains no kernels. Confirms docs/UD-QUANTS.md decision 8: no quant-kernel delta. Nothing to apply.

halo-box/strix-llama.cpp.finding: llama.cpp fork with an RDNA3.5-specific MMQ config table (ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmq-config-rdna3-5.cuh, 301 lines of tile geometry per type/J) and MTP fixes. Prefill-side (MMQ) tuning plus standard upstream C++ dispatch; no exotic decode kernel technique absent from upstream. Their speed comes from the same llama.cpp MMVQ/MMQ kernels our pinned teacher binary (17252c76) already runs.

hipengine_production_flags.note: direct resident session and public LLM path agree (public telemetry: 121-token prefill 20.4 s, decode ~253 ms/step)

e2e_gross_comparison.conclusion: hipEngine UD decode is ~3x slower than llama.cpp on the same host/file; prefill runs per-token (~169 ms/token). Decode effective weight bandwidth 59 GB/s vs llama.cpp ~178 GB/s.

gemv_leaf_bandwidth.method: production launch_gguf_linear rows=1 BF16-activation F32-output route on the largest rank-2 tensor of each quant family, 200 reps after warmup, device-synchronized wall time
gemv_leaf_bandwidth.conclusion: The raw IQ/Q3/Q4 rows=1 GEMV family runs at 23-38 GB/s while Q5_K/Q6_K paths reach 124-138 GB/s on the same host and session. The slow families dominate both published UD files (K_M: Q4_K 95 tensors; K_S: IQ4_XS 172 tensors). This is device time (~2 us dispatch floor excluded) and is the concrete decode bottleneck behind the 3x E2E gap.
gemv_leaf_bandwidth.optimization_trigger: Met: the user's 'only if super slow' rule is satisfied with 4-6x per-family headroom against the already-achieved Q5/Q6 kernel bandwidth on identical geometry.

limitations: Laptop power/clock variability: gross numbers only.
Single tensor per family, rows=1 only; prefill widths not benched here.
No kernel modifications made in this survey; optimization pass is a separate task.
